defects.rationale: Line 4 builds the 24-character token from random.randint(0, 9), whose digits come from the Mersenne Twister PRNG's predictable, globally shared state, so an attacker who requests or observes enough token output can recover that state and compute another user's reset token, enabling account takeover; use secrets.choice/token_urlsafe instead.

issues.observation: The review reports exactly one finding. A password-reset token snippet that also contains token storage, expiry, lookup, and email/response handling almost certainly exposes additional material defects (e.g., missing expiry check, token comparison without constant-time compare, token leakage in response/log, missing single-use invalidation, SQL/string-built queries). Stopping after the easiest issue (the PRNG) leaves the review incomplete.

The rationale asserts 'a 24-character token from random.randint(0, 9)' and an attacker who can 'observe enough token output' — if the snippet does not actually expose multiple tokens to the attacker, part of the exploit path is assumed rather than shown. The state-recovery claim should be grounded in what the snippet does (e.g., tokens are returned/emailed), or stated more conservatively as predictability of the generator.

revision_instructions: Re-scan the entire supplied snippet line by line and add every additional concrete defect you can anchor to a specific line — in particular check: token expiry/TTL enforcement, single-use invalidation after redemption, constant-time vs == comparison of the token, token exposure in HTTP responses or logs, query construction (string interpolation vs parameters), and any missing error/transaction handling. Add each as a separate finding with its own category and line.

Keep the existing line 4 insecure_random finding exactly as-is in category, line, and severity; only trim the rationale's exploit narrative to what the snippet actually demonstrates (predictable PRNG output used for a security-critical reset token) rather than assuming the attacker can observe many tokens.

Ensure the final output still has at most eight findings, no two findings sharing the same category+line, all line numbers within the snippet's range, and a non-empty rationale that names the concrete failure path for each.
